name: account-and-login
purpose: Sign-up, log in, password reset, delete account and the update prompt
summary:
Sign-up is four short steps: email and password (with a strength meter), a six-digit code emailed to you that the phone fills in, then name, date of birth and phone number, then a username (checked live), an optional display name and your fitness goals. Coming from a friend's invite, the sign-up knows and their tag starts the moment you join.
• Log in with email and password; the phone saves them. "Forgot password?" emails a code so you can set a new one and you're logged straight in.
• Delete account lives in Settings: one clear warning, then profile, posts, photos, messages and points go for good (Apple requires this).
• The update prompt can ask people to update if an old version ever has to stop working. It's off until needed.
• Not built yet: Apple and Google sign-in buttons (they show but do nothing), edit profile, and the help, privacy and legal pages.

name: welcome-cards
purpose: The three one-time cards that explain how Mahi works after first sign-in
summary:
Three cards after your first sign-in, shown once per account per phone:
• Post when a friend tags you. You have 48 hours to answer with a photo, front and back camera. Each answer earns you a Mahi point.
• Every post tags 3 friends. They have 48 hours to answer with a workout of their own.
• Post to open your feed. Posting your answer opens your feed for 24 hours. If a friend tags you, it locks until you answer.
The button says Next, then "Start training". There's no skip.

name: camera-and-posting
purpose: When you can post, the two-photo camera, preview, caption and location
summary:
The camera is open when you have a tag to answer, or if you've never posted (your first post is free). Otherwise the shutter is replaced by "No tags to answer. When a friend tags you, you'll have 48 hours to post." Your Mahi points sit in the corner, and a pill shows who tagged you and how long is left.
• Two taps: the first takes one side, the camera flips by itself, the second takes the other. A small window says what's next ("Selfie next"), then shows the first photo. Flip with a button or a double tap, a 0.5x wide lens where the phone has one, and hold the phone sideways for a wide photo.
• A flash button cycles off, on and auto for your view, and lights the screen for selfies. Photos are saved once at high quality, so they're sharper.
• Video (built, switched off until the next App Store build): each shot can be a photo or a video of up to 15 seconds, chosen with a Photo / Video switch or by holding the shutter. Videos play with a sound on/off button.
• Preview: your view fills the screen with the selfie in a small window. Tap to swap, drag the window to a corner, pinch to zoom. Closing asks before discarding.
• Caption up to 200 characters; typing @ brings up your friends and tags the one you pick. Location is off unless you turn it on, saved to about the nearest street block.
• Posting saves the post, its tags, deadlines, reminders and invites in one go, and the camera comes straight back. If the post answered a tag, a note says so ("Answered @sam in 3h").

name: tagging
purpose: Every post tags three friends: who can be tagged, who can't, and the nudges
summary:
Every post tags three friends, who then have 48 hours to answer. Friends are people who follow each other.
• The list greys out anyone you can't tag and says why: "tagged you, can't tag back" (you're answering their tag) or "waiting on your last tag" (they still owe you one).
• It nudges you towards friends nobody has tagged lately.
• If you haven't got three friends to tag, invite links fill the empty slots (see #invites).
• The rule that you can't tag straight back the person whose tag you're answering is what keeps the challenge reaching new people.

name: tags-and-48-hours
purpose: The 48-hour window, reminders, missed tags and cancelled tags
summary:
A tagged friend has 48 hours to post. Any post they make in that time answers every open tag they hold.
• Reminders arrive when 24 hours and 2 hours are left, never between 10pm and 7am (once push notifications are switched on).
• Missed tags are checked every five minutes. The person who tagged hears "@x missed your tag"; the person who missed hears "You missed @x's tag. Your points are back to 0." Only the two of them see it.
• Blocking someone, or an account being deleted, cancels any open tag between you along with its reminders. A cancelled tag never locks anyone's feed.

name: mahi-points
purpose: How Mahi points work, and where they show
summary:
Mahi points: every post that answers a tag on time earns one point, however many tags it answers. Miss a tag's 48 hours and your points go back to nought. Your best never goes down and always shows ("Best: 48"). Posts, the profile grid, the tag list and search say "N points".
• Only the person who answers earns: no point for the tagger, and no daily limit.
• This is not a streak (streaks are a daily thing): there is no daily streak, no training days, rest days or calendars. The only thing that counts is answering the friend who called on you.
• Only the server can change your points or best; the app can't.

name: feed
purpose: The feed of friends' workouts: what's in it and how the cards work
summary:
Your friends' workouts and your own, full screen, one at a time, newest first. Pull down to refresh, and it keeps loading as you go.
• Each card shows the tagged friends' bubbles, the poster's points after that post, who answered whom and how fast, the time and the caption with tagged names you can tap. The selfie window swaps and drags like it does in the camera.
• The like and comment buttons sit higher up the right side, on a shade that runs edge to edge. Press and hold a post to hide everything but the photo; let go to bring it back.
• Tapping any avatar opens that person's profile.

name: feed-lock
purpose: When the feed is open, when it locks, and what it says
summary:
Posting opens your feed for 24 hours. If you're tagged in that time, the feed locks when the 24 hours end. If you're not, it stays open until someone tags you, and then it locks until you post your answer.
• A new person starts locked. Miss a tag and it stays locked until a friend tags you again.
• While locked, friends' photos and captions are hidden on the server, not just on the phone. Your own posts always show.
• A locked feed says who tagged you and how long you've got, or that you can post again when a friend tags you. An open feed says how long it stays open, or warns "locks in N hours unless you post your answer".

name: likes-and-comments
purpose: Likes, double tap to like, and the comments sheet
summary:
Tap the heart or double tap the photo to like (double tap only likes, never unlikes). Counts update live.
• Comments open in a full-height sheet titled "N comments", oldest first, and update live. Comments can't be edited or deleted yet.
• Each comment has a heart and a count; tap the count to see who liked it and open their profiles.
• Posts opened from a profile look exactly like the feed, with likes and comments.

name: profiles
purpose: Your profile, other people's profiles, and Settings
summary:
Your profile: your photo (tap to open it full screen and pinch to zoom, + to change it), name and handle, your friends list, and two numbers: Points and Best. Below that, "Suggested for you" folded away, and a grid of every post.
• Other people: their photo, friends list, Points and Best, a Follow button and a Message button. Their grid only opens if you follow them and your feed is open. A menu lets you block or report them.
• Profiles scroll as one page, so the header moves away and the grid fills the screen. Tap a post to scroll up and down through all of that person's posts; swipe sideways to close.
• Settings: blocked users (with unblock), delete account, log out and the version line. A light/dark switch sits on your profile; the camera is always dark.
• Not built yet: edit profile, and changing your name or username after sign-up.

name: friends-and-suggestions
purpose: Following, who counts as a friend, and "Suggested for you"
summary:
Follow anyone. Friends are people who follow each other, and only friends can be tagged. The friends list shows names, never numbers.
• "Suggested for you" shows friends of friends, ranked by how many people you share. Someone new sees popular people instead. It skips people you already follow and anyone blocked either way.

name: search-people
purpose: Finding people by name or username
summary: Tap the magnifier on your profile or in Messages, or "Find friends" on an empty feed, to get a frosted full-screen search. It matches part of a username, display name, first name or last name, and shows points. Blocked people are hidden. Tapping a result opens their profile, where you can follow or message them.

name: messages
purpose: Private chats and message requests
summary:
Private chats that update live, with day headers and older messages loading as you scroll up. Opening a chat marks it read; a failed send puts your text back in the box.
• Every new chat starts as a request until the other person accepts it, even between friends. Turning one down asks first. Your own outgoing requests show as Pending.
• Blocking stops all messages both ways.

name: notifications
purpose: The bell and the notifications list
summary:
The bell lists likes, comments, follows, tags, answered tags, missed tags, points lost to a missed tag and friends who joined from your invite, with unread dots. Closing the list marks everything read; blocked people are filtered out.
• Each line uses the same words as the alert on the phone for the same thing. A tag reads "You've been tagged by @sam. 48 hours to post your Mahi!".
• Tapping the avatar opens their profile. Not built yet: tapping a post notice to open that post.

name: push-notifications
purpose: Alerts on the phone: built, waiting to be switched on
summary:
Alerts on the phone. Built and waiting to be switched on; nothing is sent yet.
• Asking: a full-screen page, once per phone, after the welcome cards: "When do you post on Mahi?", one line of why, and a card "Please turn on notifications" with Allow and Not now. Someone who says no sees a small line on the camera the next time a friend tags them, "Turn on notifications so you never miss a tag", which opens the phone's Settings. It can be dismissed until the next tag.
• Tagged: "You've just been tagged by @sam. 48 hours left to post your Mahi!" Reminders 24 hours and 2 hours before the deadline: "24 hours left to post your Mahi! @sam is waiting."
• Feed: "Your feed locks in 1 hour. Post your answer to @sam to keep it open." an hour before an open feed locks, and "Your feed is locked. Post your answer to @sam to open it." when it does. Only for someone who has been tagged, and taken back if they post first. Each can be switched off and the hour can be changed.
• Also: "@sam answered your tag in 3h", "@sam missed your tag", "You missed @sam's tag. Your points are back to 0.", likes, comments, follows, a friend joining from your invite and new messages.
• Quiet hours are 10pm to 7am in each person's own time zone; anything due then waits until 7am, and several at once are grouped. An alert that is more than an hour late is dropped rather than sent with the wrong time on it.
• Tapping an alert: a follow or a joined invite opens the profile; a tag, a reminder or a feed alert opens the camera; a message opens Messages; everything else opens the notifications list.
• Works on the app people have now: no new App Store build needed for iPhone. Still to do: check the Apple push key, switch on the sending service, then turn the page on, first for one phone as a test. Android comes later. The wording is waiting for the founder's OK.

name: moderation-safety
purpose: Block, report and banned accounts
summary:
Block asks first, then removes follows both ways, hides each other's posts and profiles, cancels any open tag between you and freezes the chat. Unblocking restores the chat; you'd need to follow each other again.
• Report: spam, harassment, inappropriate content, impersonation or other, once per person. There's no tool to review reports yet.
• Banned accounts are set by hand on the server: they're signed out and disappear from feeds, friends lists, tagging and reminders.

name: invites
purpose: Invite links and six-character codes for friends who aren't on Mahi yet
summary:
Each empty tag slot becomes a one-use link and a six-character code that last seven days. Whoever joins with it becomes your friend straight away, gets their 48 hours, and you hear they joined.
• The share message reads "I tagged you on Mahi — you've got 48 hours to post back" plus the link. After posting, a list shows each invite and whether it's been sent.
• Not working end to end yet: the invite website (togethermahi.com) isn't set up, and the code isn't shown anywhere yet, so until that page exists an invite can't be used.

name: navigation-and-design
purpose: Swipes, the glass bar, sheets, fonts, colours and the design values
summary:
Mahi opens on the camera, and the other screens sit beside it in one row: the feed, then your profile, then messages. Swipe left to move along the row and right to come back; there is no up or down swiping. Pages snap into place with a light tap you can feel.
• On the newest App Store build, the phone's own tab bar sits along the bottom in the same order: tap a tab to jump there, and it follows your swipes. Older builds have a floating glass bar on the left of the camera instead; hold and drag along it to switch. Sheets slide up and swipe down to close; menus and date pickers are the iPhone's own; passwords and codes fill themselves in.
• Inter font throughout, all wording in sentence case. Calm off-white and off-black with a cyan accent for anything you can tap and gold for points, in light and dark mode. Every colour, size and spacing comes from one shared set of values, so the app and the website stay consistent.
• Apple's own icons come with the next App Store build.

name: server-and-numbers
purpose: Rules enforced on the server, time zones, and the figures only we can see
summary:
Who can post, the three tags, the 48 hours, the Mahi points and the feed lock are all enforced on the server, so an old or tampered app can't get round them. Posting is all or nothing, and a retry never makes a duplicate.
• Every post is dated in the poster's own local day, and quiet hours follow their clock.
• Our numbers, read only by us: tags sent, answered and missed with the typical answer time; posts and posters; invites sent and claimed; and how many accounts posted each week.

name: waitlist-website
purpose: The one-page waitlist site and its sign-up form
summary:
One page: what Mahi is, how it works in three steps (post when a friend tags you, every post tags three friends, every answer earns a Mahi point), and a form for name, email, how you train and whether you'd test early versions. Sign-ups land in a list with an email alert each.
• The site only rebuilds when we ask it to, by editing one file in the repo.

name: analytics-posthog
purpose: What we measure in PostHog and the feature switches
summary:
Counted: sign-ups and log-ins, password resets, tags sent, answered and missed, points lost, invites shared and claimed, feed unlocks, pushes opened, blocks and reports.
• Fifteen feature switches can turn a feature off from outside the app without an update, in case one misbehaves. Every switch in PostHog matches one the app reads; the unused ones were deleted on 1 October 2026.
• Crashes go to Sentry, but only from builds marked production.

name: apple-ios-store
purpose: App Store builds, TestFlight, review notes and what Apple requires
summary: Nothing is in the App Store yet; updates go to our three registered test iPhones. Use this channel for App Store builds, review feedback and Apple's requirements (in-app delete account is already built for that).

name: android-play-store
purpose: Android builds and Play Store listing
summary: Android has never been built yet; the app and the site say "Coming to iPhone and Android". Use this channel for the first Android build, device testing and the Play Store listing.

name: ota-updates
purpose: Over-the-air updates: what went out, when, and how to check it on a phone
summary:
Most changes reach phones as an over-the-air update without an App Store release. The Settings version line shows the build and update number (for example 10.22). To check an update landed: force-quit and open the app twice.
• Post each update here with its number and what changed.

name: maintenance
purpose: Bugs, crashes, server upkeep and anything that needs fixing
summary: Report anything broken here with the phone, the version line from Settings, and what you were doing. Server-side checks and database changes are recorded here too.

name: repo-structure
purpose: How the code and the project are organised
summary: One repository: the iPhone app, the website and the server rules together, with automated tests for all three (over 1,300 app checks and 300 database checks). The rules of the road for working in it live in the repo's own docs.

name: project-planning-strategy
purpose: Product decisions, priorities and what's next
summary: Decisions that shape the product live here. Decided so far: post only when tagged (never to show off), Mahi points (one per post that answers a tag, back to nought on a missed tag, best always visible; not a streak, and no daily streak for now), no rest days or calendars, and the 24-hour feed rule. Open: what happens to a flagged post, the invite website, push notifications setup, Android.

name: feature-flags
purpose: Every app switch, what it controls, and whether it's on, off or partly rolled out
summary:
Every switch in the app, what it does, and who has it. Change them in PostHog, on its switches page; a switch that isn't in PostHog counts as off.
• `onboarding-welcome-cards` — Three welcome cards after first sign-in, also under Settings → Help. *On for everyone (100%).*
• `auth-password-reset` — "Forgot password?" emails a code to set a new one. *On for everyone (100%).*
• `account-delete` — Delete account in Settings. *On for everyone (100%).*
• `auth-apple-signin` — "Continue with Apple" (does nothing yet). *On (100%); should be off until built.*
• `auth-google-signin` — "Continue with Google" (does nothing yet). *On (100%); should be off until built.*
• `camera-pip-guide` — Camera's small window: "Selfie next", then the first photo. *On for everyone (100%).*
• `comment-likes` — Heart and count on each comment, and who liked it. *On for everyone (100%).*
• `ios-sf-symbols` — Apple's own icons on iPhone. *Off until the next App Store build.*
• `context-menu-preview` — Hold a post, profile square or chat to pop it up with a menu. *Off until the next App Store build.*
• `camera-tap-focus` — Tap the camera to focus and set brightness there. *Off until the next App Store build.*
• `identity-verification` — Didit identity and age checks. *Off until the next App Store build and the Didit account are ready.*
• `purchases` — Subscriptions and in-app purchases through RevenueCat. *Off until the next App Store build and RevenueCat are ready.*
• `video-posts` — Each shot can be a photo or a video (up to 15 seconds), with sound on/off. *Off for everyone. Needs the next App Store build first.*
• `tags-invite-step` — "Invite 3 friends to post" step and the sent/not sent invite list. *On for everyone (100%).*
• `tag-slots` — One tag screen: slots that show where each tag is at, in-app invites, links sent on tap. *Off (not created). After the database change and a phone check.*
• `invite-links` — Invite buttons on the tag screen and after posting. *On for everyone (100%).*
• `tag-challenges` — Open-tags banner on the camera. *On for everyone (100%).*
• `feed-lock-explainer` — Locked feed says who tagged you; open feed says how long it stays open. *On for everyone (100%).*
• `notifications-core` — The notifications bell and list. *On for everyone (100%).*
• `push-core` — The full-screen "turn on notifications" page and the camera's reminder line. *Off (not created). Goes on once the sending service is live and tested on one phone.*
• `nav-glass-rail` — Floating glass bar on the camera only, with Camera, Feed, Messages and Profile. *On for everyone (100%).*
• `nav-rail-morph` — Glass bar as one pill with a sliding selector; hold and drag to switch. *On for everyone (100%).*
Last checked 2 October 2026, 15:00.

name: apple-icons
purpose: Apple's own icon set on iPhone
summary: Mahi's icons switch to Apple's own symbols on iPhone, so they match the rest of the phone and scale with the text size people choose. Android keeps today's icons. Ships in the next App Store build and stays switched off until we turn it on.

name: hold-to-preview
purpose: Hold to pop a post or chat up for a quick look
summary: Hold a post in the feed, a square on a profile, or a chat in Messages, and it pops up over a blurred background with a short menu underneath, the way iPhone apps do. On the feed this replaces holding to see just the photo. Ships in the next App Store build and stays switched off until we turn it on.

name: camera-features
purpose: Flash, tap to focus, better photos and stronger feedback
summary: Flash for your view and a bright-screen flash for selfies, sharper photos, steadier video and clearer vibrations are already live for everyone. Tap to focus and set brightness where you tap comes with the next App Store build and stays switched off until we turn it on.

name: identity-verification
purpose: Checking people are who they say they are (Didit)
summary: Lets Mahi confirm a person's identity or age with a quick ID and face check through Didit, for example before someone can post or message. The parts that need the App Store go into the next build and stay switched off; turning it on later is an update, once we decide where it applies and set up the Didit account.

name: subscriptions
purpose: Paid plans and in-app purchases (RevenueCat)
summary: Gets Mahi ready to sell subscriptions or one-off purchases through the App Store, managed with RevenueCat. The parts that need the App Store go into the next build and stay switched off; turning it on later is an update, once the plans, prices and RevenueCat account are set up.

name: haptics
purpose: How Mahi feels in the hand: every vibration and what it means
summary: Mahi gives a small, distinct vibration at the moments that matter: a crisp click on the shutter, a soft one when the camera flips, a confirmation when a post and its tags send, a stronger bump when you earn a Mahi point, a warning when your feed locks and a success when it opens again, a light tick for likes and switching screens, and a buzz when something fails. Every vibration goes through one shared set, so the same moment always feels the same everywhere.

name: questions-and-answers
purpose: Questions the team needs to answer before something is built or switched on
summary: Each question is its own message, with the choices to pick from. Answer in its thread; once it's decided it goes into the decisions list and the work goes ahead.
